text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: api-gateway 5xx rate spike detected > 4% (5m) - auto-created incident INC-2026-0315-DBEGG. Source: datadog. Follow the incident page: https://incidents.redwood.example/INC-2026-0315-DBEGG

lucy: Oncall here. Seeing a sudden jump to 502/504s, mostly from east-1 and eu-west-1. Im pulling traces now.

ryan: Im seeing upstream errors tagged `egress:provider-x` in the logs. Connection reset + TLS handshake failures approx at 08:42 UTC.

priya: Query I ran in Datadog: `avg(last_5m):sum:requests.errors{service:api-gateway,code:5xx}.as_count() / sum:requests.total{service:api-gateway}.as_count() > 0.04`

infra-bot: Snapshot: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/xyz/api-errors?from=now-30m&to=now -- top downstream: provider-x, provider-y.

lucy: customer impact: intermittent for users on embedding-heavy endpoints and realtime streams. Support reports 3 active tickets.

ryan: repro: curl to gateway with model streaming shows long `TLS handshake` logs when traffic routes to provider-x IPs.

priya: temporary mitigation options: 1) route around provider-x by toggling egress policy -> provider-fallback, 2) raise gateway upstream timeouts to avoid retry storms, 3) add short-lived circuit-breaker for any single downstream raising >20% errors in 2m.

lucy: I can flip routing to provider-fallback for a subset of traffic (10%) to validate. Prefer that over global timeout change.

ryan: FYI making routing change via feature-flag. Command: ```
kubectl -n infra exec -it ffctl -- patch featureflag egress-routing -p '{"spec":{"weights":{"provider-x":0.9,"provider-fallback":0.1}}}'
```

infra-bot: Feature flag rollout started for 10% traffic, canary logs: https://logs.redwood.example/ff/egress/rollout/1819994322

priya: While canary runs, we should tune alerting. This monitor has paged nights for tiny blips before. Proposal: change pager thresholds to two-tier: pager if >5% 5m OR >3% sustained 15m. For 3-5% send Slack-only to #eng-oncall. Also add an exclusion for `route:healthcheck` and `env:staging`.

lucy: agree. Also add a tag-based override: if `customer_impact:true` then always page regardless of threshold.

ryan: quick note: the current monitor uses global 5xx rate which conflates provider-specific vs app-bug. Add per-upstream monitors for provider-x/provider-fallback so we can page only when a downstream provider is flapping.

priya: good call. I'll open the monitor edits and create two new monitors: `prod.api.5xx_rate.provider-x` and `prod.api.5xx_rate.provider-fallback`. Suggestions for thresholds in the monitor description.

infra-bot: Temporarily silencing `prod.api.5xx_rate` pager for 30m while mitigation in progress. Suppression reason: ongoing egress routing canary. Will still post to slack. Suppression expires 2026-03-15T09:30:00Z.

lucy: the 10% canary to provider-fallback reduced errors for that slice by ~70%. Rolling to 50% now.

ryan: provider-x team contacted. They report intermittent upstream proxy restarts in their fleet (observed on their side) and are deploying a fix. ETA 15-25m.

priya: required post-incident followups (tentative):
- codify per-upstream 95/99 latency + 5xx dashboard panels on `api/overview`
- create circuit-breaker metric and add graphs for fallback activation counts
- update runbook `oncall/egress-failover.md` with step-by-step for FF rollback and blocker checks
- make monitor change permanent with rationale and PR link

lucy: adding to infra board now. Ticket INFRA-4521.

infra-bot: Handoff note: lucy -> tina at 2026-03-15T09:00Z UTC. Current status: canary routing applied, provider-x rolling fix, suppression active until 09:30Z, 3 support tickets open.

tina: taking handoff. Ill watch for any regression and will un-suppress if we see customer noise. Also will post a short summary to #customer-impact for CS.

ryan: follow-up monitoring tweak idea: instead of a single global 5xx rate, add these monitors: per-region 5xx (us/eu/asia), per-upstream 5xx (provider-x, provider-fallback), and an anomaly detector on `rate_of_change` to avoid alerting for gradual trends only.

priya: on runbook/permissions: add a line specifying who can apply ephemeral suppressions and TTL defaults. Right now too many people suppress without documentation.

lucy: agree. Also add an alert for `upstream_connect_timeouts` specifically (counts of `connect_timeout` tags) and a small playbook for when to enable fallback route vs. change timeouts.

infra-bot: Incident update: mitigation working, error rate trending down to ~1.1% overall. provider-x reporting successful rollout. Next update at 2026-03-15T09:15Z.

tina: thanks all. Will coordinate the postmortem doc and assign owners for the follow-ups. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: status -> monitoring (no active customer escalations). Closing incident page in 24h pending postmortem and action items.

lucy: closing notes: root cause likely provider-x transient proxy restarts + overly-broad pager thresholds. Immediate actions: egress canary, temporary suppression, new per-upstream monitors. Follow-ups: dashboards, runbook updates, permanent monitor changes.

priya: logging assigned owners and ETA in INFRA-4521.

ryan: cheers team, nice quick coordination.
